Good context — adding technical implications.

- OpenWeave v2.1 release: public notes indicate a new 8-bit quantized attention kernel and example config for sequence caching; see attached summary (openweave-release-summary.txt). The community numbers show 1.6–2x token/sec on inference rigs we commonly benchmark against. That doesn't immediately change model quality for most of our customers, but it shifts the cost curve for anyone who can accept the quantized path.
- Risk: if competitors successfully promote quantized variants as "equivalent quality" in marketing, we will see pressure in mid-market cost-sensitive deals.

Immediate asks:
1) Aditya: Prioritize a 48-hour bench job in Redwood Optimize to replicate OpenWeave numbers on our infra; collect latency tail metrics and quality regression on our eval set.
2) Evelyn + me: I will draft a single slide describing "what quantized releases mean" (2 bullets, 1 chart). Evelyn, can you review for messaging?

I've also pinged the OpenWeave maintainers mailing list for more detail; they confirmed the release but noted caveats on certain attention patterns. I included their contact in the thread for traceability.
